correction.text: Egypt from Aswan to the Mediterranean reunified under Ahmose I: 'he successfully defeated the Hyksos in Lower Egypt, reuniting the Two Lands'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first New Kingdom shape begins in -1500, but the Eighteenth Dynasty reunites the Two Lands c. 1550. The shape is the Nile Valley from the First Cataract to the Delta; Gaza (Sharuhen, from -1547) and Lower Nubia (from -1540) are added by ledger events, and Nubia to the Fourth Cataract by -1504. The NK page's infobox gives no area (only a 3-5 million population for the 13th century BC), so Cliopatria's areas cannot be checked against it.

correction.text: the shape as drawn, for -1504..-1458: Egypt, Nubia to the Fourth Cataract and the Gaza coast; Canaan and Syria are added from 1457 by new keyframes -1457 and the ledger

keyframe_review.note: -1500..-1401, 635,790 km2, bbox 18.1-31.7 N, 27.7-34.9 E. The southern half is right: 'Around 1500 BC, Nubia was absorbed into the New Kingdom of Egypt' (annexation c. 1504 BC) and Thutmose III's furthest point in Nubia was the Fourth Cataract, the shape's southern edge (Thutmose III page: 'In Year 50, Thutmose III waged his last military campaign. He attacked Nubia, but only went so far as the fourth cataract of the Nile'; the Kingdom of Kush page gives the annexation, not the Year 50 sentence). The northern edge at Gaza is Sharuhen. The shape does not carry Thutmose III's Canaan (from the Megiddo year, 1457) or Syria (1447), which Cliopatria draws only from -1400: the shape is right for -1504..-1458 only.

union.text: Egypt and Nubia as in the -1500 shape
the Canaanite city-states after Megiddo, 'forcing the Syrian princes to send tribute and noble hostages to Egypt'

correction.text: the -1500 shape plus Canaan (Megiddo and the princes who paid tribute), as vassal tint under the ledger's vassal events

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, -1457..-1448: the -1500 shape plus Canaan after Megiddo ('Year 23, I Shemu day 21', which 'corresponds to 9 May 1457 BC'), the Canaanite princes paying tribute. Simyra on the Syrian coast follows in Thutmose's year 30 (1450) and the Euphrates in year 33 (1447); the ledger adds them.

minus.text: the Aleppo region around Aleppo and Carchemish, 'still unconquered' in year 33 and the ground where Mitanni 'engaged the Egyptians' in year 35: never Egyptian

correction.text: the Thutmose III shape without the Aleppo region, valid -1447..-1353 (Aleppo was never Egyptian, so there is no loss to Mitanni); from -1352 see keyframe -1352

keyframe_review.note: -1400..-1301, 708,814 km2, bbox to 36.6 N, 36.9 E: Thutmose III's greatest extent ('an empire stretching from the Asian regions of Syria in the North, to Upper Nubia in the south'; NK page: 'conquered much of the Near East from the Euphrates to Nubia'). It is right from 1447 (the Euphrates crossing, year 33) but not for the whole century and a half Cliopatria gives it: the NK page says 'Egypt had not held Kadesh since the time of Akhenaten', so the Syrian cities go in the Akhenaten age (ledger -1352). The Kadesh page's sentence that Egypt 'continued to lose territory to the Mitanni in northern Syria' under Thutmose IV and Amenhotep III is undated and carries 'citation needed'; the Amenhotep III page records no territorial loss (marriages to Gilukhepa in regnal year 10 and Tadukhepa about year 36) and the Mitanni page says Thutmose IV 'would eventually make peace with the Mitannians', so the former ledger loss of -1400 is removed. No area figure on the pages opened. [Author fix me-03-b, 2026-10-18] Aleppo and Carchemish: Thutmose III page, year 33 ('the still unconquered cities of Aleppo and Carchemish') and year 35 (Mitanni 'engaged the Egyptians around Aleppo'); the former wording 'undated loss to Mitanni' is gone.

union.text: Egypt and Nubia as in the -1500 shape
Canaan, the one Asian region the Kadesh page leaves to Egypt after 1274

correction.text: the -1500 shape plus Canaan as vassal tint

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, -1352..-1276: Egypt, Nubia and Canaan, without Syria north of Canaan. NK page: 'Egypt had not held Kadesh since the time of Akhenaten' (capital at Amarna from c. 1352); Kadesh page: after the 1274 battle 'Egypt's sphere of influence in Asia was now restricted to Canaan'. The page is silent on Seti I's dates, so his capture of Kadesh and Amurru ('a second campaign led to his capture of Kadesh and the Amurru kingdom'; 'at some point, both regions may have lapsed back under Hittite control') is not drawn.

correction.text: Egypt, Nubia, Canaan and the Orontes/Amurru lands up to Kadesh, held for 1275-1274 only

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, -1275..-1274: Ramesses II's fourth year ('marched north into Syria to recapture Amurru', c. 1275 BC) to the Battle of Kadesh (May 1274 BC), after which 'the Hittites were routed, but they held on to Kadesh'. The Orontes and Amurru land is the -1300 Cliopatria shape, which reaches 34.6 N.

union.text: Egypt and Nubia as in the -1500 shape
Canaan, Egypt's Asian sphere after Kadesh

correction.text: the -1500 shape plus Canaan as vassal tint, for -1300..-1241: the Syrian lands of Cliopatria's -1300 shape (Amurru, Kadesh, the Orontes) are drawn only by keyframe -1275 for -1275..-1274

keyframe_review.note: -1300..-1241, 700,581 km2, bbox to 34.6 N: the Syrian part (Amurru, Kadesh) is held only in 1275-1274 on the pages opened. Before 1275 the Hittites hold it (Egypt 'had not held Kadesh since the time of Akhenaten'); after the 1274 battle 'Egypt's sphere of influence in Asia was now restricted to Canaan'. Use keyframes -1352, -1275 and -1273 instead. fx-46 (request R020): the correction used to be Cliopatria's -1300 shape itself, so the compiler (which draws the correction of a 'wrong' entry like any other) went on drawing the 61 Syrian and Lebanese cells (35.3-36.9 E, 30.6-34.4 N) that this entry says not to use, in the union with keyframes -1352, -1275 and -1273. The correction is now the same Egypt+Nubia+Canaan spec as keyframes -1352 and -1273, so it adds nothing to either. Battle of Kadesh page: 'Egypt's sphere of influence in Asia was now restricted to Canaan' (after 1274); 'Egyptian influence over Amurru and Qadesh seems to have been lost forever'.

union.text: Egypt and Nubia as in the -1500 shape

correction.text: the -1500 shape plus Canaan as vassal tint

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, -1273..-1201: after Kadesh and the 21st-year treaty with Hattusili III (1258 BC), which 'concluded the borderland conflicts', Egypt keeps Canaan and Nubia; Amurru 'seems to have been lost forever'. Ramesses II's raids on Dapur and Tunip in his eighth and ninth years (c. 1271-1270) held ground for under a year ('Within a year, it had returned to Hittite control').

correction.text: do not use for -1240..-1151; Syria north of Canaan is Hittite (keyframes -1273 and -1200)

keyframe_review.note: -1240..-1151, same 700,581 km2 shape as -1300: it still holds Amurru and Kadesh (34.6 N) for 90 years after the Kadesh page says they stayed Hittite. Use keyframes -1273, -1200 and the ledger.

minus.text: the Dongola Reach, south of 20 N

correction.text: Egypt, Nubia north of the Dongola Reach, and Canaan as vassal tint, valid -1200..-1137

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, -1200..-1151: the Kingdom of Kush page says 'By 1200 BC, Egyptian involvement in the Dongola Reach was nonexistent', so Nubia south of about 20 N goes. Canaan stays in the Egyptian sphere (the 20th Dynasty settled the defeated Sea Peoples 'in Southern Canaan'; 'Egyptian presence in the Levant is still attested as far as Byblos', NK page). [Author fix me-03-b, 2026-10-18] Ends -1137 (was -1151): the Ramesses VI page dates the end of Egyptian Canaan to 'during or soon after' that reign (c.1144-1136 BC), see ledger -1136; the Cliopatria -1150 shape has no Canaan, so this keyframe stands in for -1150..-1137.

union.text: the Dongola Reach, south of 20 N
Gaza and Sharuhen, the Gaza coast at the north edge of the Cliopatria -1150 shape

minus.text: the Dongola Reach south of 20 N and the Gaza coast

correction.text: valid -1136..-1078 without the Dongola Reach and the Gaza coast (Egyptian Palestine ended c. 1136); for -1150..-1137 use keyframe -1200; not for -1077 onward

keyframe_review.note: -1150..-1001, 635,996 km2, bbox 18.1-31.7 N, 27.7-34.9 E (Egypt, Sudan, Israel): the same footprint as -1500. Right for -1150..-1078 only if the Dongola Reach is removed ('By 1200 BC, Egyptian involvement in the Dongola Reach was nonexistent'). From 1077 the Delta (Tanis) and Thebes are the 21st Dynasty and its priests, and Kush is independent 'around 1070 BC': see the 21st Dynasty dossier's keyframes. Ramesses VI page: 'Egyptian presence in Canaan was terminated during or soon after Ramesses VI's rule' (reign c.1144-1136 BC), with 'the last garrisons leaving southern and western Palestine', so the Gaza coast of this shape is removed from -1136 (ledger -1136).

region.text: Thebes and Upper Egypt up to Cusae

ledger.note: c. 1550: Ahmose I of Thebes founds the Eighteenth Dynasty and the New Kingdom. 'Ahmose ... was the founder of the Eighteenth Dynasty of Egypt'; Thebes 'became the capital for the whole of Egypt'. Dates differ by page: reign 1570-1546, 1560-1537, 1551-1527 or 1539-1514 BC (Ahmose I), 'Rise: c. 1570 BC' (NK infobox); the 15th and 17th Dynasty infoboxes end c. 1550 and the Kadesh page says 'around 1550 BC'.

region.text: Avaris, Memphis and the Hyksos Delta

ledger.note: c. 1550: Ahmose I takes Avaris and ends Hyksos rule in Egypt. 'These records indicate that Ahmose I led three attacks against Avaris' ... 'in the fourth attack, he conquered the city'; 'Ahmose would have conquered Avaris by the 18th or 19th year of his reign at the very latest'. The Seventeenth Dynasty page has a conflicting 'In 1559 BC, led by ... Ahmose I, they conquered the city of Memphis. Then, with naval support, conquered Hutwaret', not drawn (see notes).

region.text: Sharuhen near Gaza, the last Hyksos stronghold

ledger.note: c. 1547: Ahmose I takes Sharuhen. 'conquering their stronghold Sharuhen near Gaza after a three-year siege'. The page gives no year for the siege; -1547 bridges three years from the fall of Avaris (page silent). [Author fix me-03-b, 2026-10-18] Sharuhen page (tried for the thin item): 'The armies of Pharaoh Ahmose I seized and razed the town after a three-year siege'; no year, no tie to the fall of Avaris, so the date stays a bridge at confidence 1 (the Hyksos dossier hands Sharuhen over in -1550; one of the two must change at the merge).

region.text: Lower Nubia (Wawat) with the administrative centre at Buhen

ledger.note: c. 1540: Ahmose I restores Egyptian rule over Lower Nubia from Buhen. 'Ahmose restored Egyptian rule over Nubia, which was controlled from a new administrative center established at Buhen'; Aata and Tetian rebel and are crushed. No year on the page; -1540 sits inside the reign (page silent). Kamose had campaigned against the Kushites and may have targeted the fortress at Buhen (Kamose page). [Author fix me-03-b, 2026-10-18] Buhen page: the Kushites 'captured Buhen during the 13th Dynasty' and held it 'until Ahmose I recaptured it at the beginning of the 18th Dynasty' (no year); Viceroy of Kush page: silent on Ahmose I and Buhen ('Possibly the first viceroy': Si-Tayit under Ahmose I). Still confidence 1. The Kingdom of Kerma dossier (af-01-x) holds Lower Nubia to -1504 on the Kerma page ('controlled the 1st to 4th Cataracts'): the pages disagree and one dossier must change.

region.text: Nubia up to the Fourth Cataract: the Kerma kingdom's valley 'between the first and fourth cataracts'

ledger.note: c. 1504: Thutmose I annexes Nubia. 'Thutmose I occupied Kush and destroyed its capital, Kerma'; 'annexation of Nubia c. 1504 BC'; 'Around 1500 BC, Nubia was absorbed into the New Kingdom of Egypt'. The Fourth Cataract is the southern limit (Thutmose III, year 50: 'only went so far as the fourth cataract of the Nile').

region.text: Megiddo and the city-states of Canaan whose princes sent tribute and hostages

ledger.note: May 1457: Thutmose III takes Megiddo and the Canaanite princes pay tribute. 'Year 23, I Shemu [day] 21' = 9 May 1457 BC; 'Thutmose was forced to besiege the city, and finally took it after a siege of seven or eight months'; 'forcing the Syrian princes to send tribute and noble hostages to Egypt'. The page says 'Syrian princes', the region is the reading of the Megiddo plain and Canaan.

region.text: Syria from the Phoenician coast (Simyra) to the Orontes, without the Aleppo region: the -1400 shape without the -1500 shape and Aleppo

ledger.note: 1447: Thutmose III reaches the Euphrates. Year 33: 'after Thutmose III had taken control of the Syrian cities' he crossed the Euphrates against Mitanni and 'put up a second stele commemorating his crossing'; Simyra had fallen in year 30 (1450: 'Turning west again, Thutmose took Simyra'). Calendar years counted from the page's accession of 1479 BC (year 23 = 1457). The Syrian cities are drawn as tributaries; the page does not say they were annexed. [Author fix me-03-b, 2026-10-18] Region was the -1400 shape without the -1500 shape, which reaches 36.6 N and takes in part of the Aleppo region. Thutmose III page (re-read): in year 33 he 'continued north through the territory belonging to the still unconquered cities of Aleppo and Carchemish' and in year 35 the king of Mitanni 'engaged the Egyptians around Aleppo' (a boasted victory that 'raises suspicion'), so the Aleppo region is subtracted. Mitanni page (re-read): 'a more or less permanent border between Egypt and Mitanni seems to have existed near Qatna on the Orontes River' and Aleppo was 'incorporated into Mitanni'; read strictly that would cut the tint south of Qatna (34.8 N), but the sentence is undated and about the later border, so it is not drawn here; flagged for the Mitanni and Hittite batch (me-04).

region.text: the Aleppo region, where the Mitanni army engaged the Egyptians

ledger.note: 1445: Mitanni meets Thutmose at Aleppo. 'By Thutmose's 35th year, the king of Mitanni had raised a large army and engaged the Egyptians around Aleppo'; 'the Assyrian, Babylonian and Hittite kings honored Thutmose with gifts'. Year 35 = 1445 by the page's accession year.

1438: Thutmose III's last recorded Syrian campaign. The page's year-42 campaign 'engaged and destroyed three surrounding Mitannian garrisons' but 'he did not take Kadesh'; it says nothing of a treaty, so the end of the contest is bridged to this last dated campaign (year 42 = 1438). [Author fix me-03-b, 2026-10-18] Mitanni page (tried for the thin item): 'Amenhotep II fought in Syria in 1425 BC, presumably against Mitanni as well, but did not reach the Euphrates'; 'Amenhotep II's son, Thutmose IV, would eventually make peace with the Mitannians' (no year); a marriage alliance followed (Gilukhepa, Amenhotep III regnal year 10, Amenhotep III page). No page dates the end of the contest, so -1438 stays at confidence 1.
c. 1352: Akhenaten moves the capital to Amarna (Akhetaten). Infobox: 'Amarna c. 1352-1336 BC Akhenaten of Dynasty XVIII'.

region.text: Syria north of Canaan, from the coast at Simyra to Kadesh, without the Aleppo region

ledger.note: c. 1352: the Syrian cities are lost. 'Egypt had not held Kadesh since the time of Akhenaten' and 'the Hittites had gradually extended their influence into the Levant'. The page gives no year; -1352 is Akhenaten's accession as the infobox dates the Amarna capital (bridging). [Reviewer me-03-b, 2026-10-18] Region was 'Levant' (Syria, Lebanon, Israel, Palestine, Jordan, Hatay), which would also end the Canaan tint that keyframe -1352 keeps; now the -1400 shape without the -1500 shape and Canaan, as the text says. [Author fix me-03-b, 2026-10-18] Region follows ledger -1447 (Aleppo subtracted). Seti I page (tried for the thin item): he took 'the Syrian town of Kadesh and neighbouring territory of Amurru from the Hittite Empire' (reign 1290-1279 BC) and 'Kadesh, however, soon reverted to Hittite control', no dates for the capture or the reversion, so it is not drawn; the Mitanni page dates the Hittite subjugation of Aleppo, Mukish, Niya, Arahtu, Qatna and Nuhashshe to 1345 BC. The loss of the Syrian cities stays a bridge to Akhenaten's accession at confidence 1.
c. 1336: the court returns to Thebes. Infobox: 'Thebes c. 1336-1279 BC Dynasty XVIII and Dynasty XIX (until Ramesses II)'.
1295: the Nineteenth Dynasty begins. NK page: 'the Nineteenth Dynasty (1295-1189 BC)'. Same state, same colour (rule 2).
c. 1279: Ramesses II moves the capital to Pi-Ramesses. Infobox: 'Pi-Ramesses c. 1279-1213 BC Ramesses II of Dynasty XIX'.

region.text: Amurru and the Orontes valley up to Kadesh (Homs, Tartus and north Lebanon)

ledger.note: c. 1275: Ramesses II retakes Amurru. In his fourth year he 'marched north into Syria to recapture Amurru' (c. 1275 BC); the page notes Seti I's earlier capture of Kadesh and Amurru and that 'both regions may have lapsed back under Hittite control'.

region.text: Kadesh and Amurru on the Orontes

ledger.note: 1275: Egyptians and Hittites fight for the Orontes. The first campaign that holds ground is Ramesses II's recovery of Amurru in his fourth year; the zone is the Lebanon-Syria border along which the battle was fought ('along what is today the Lebanon-Syria border').

May 1274: Kadesh is fought and Egypt withdraws to Canaan. 'The battle occurred on Year 5 III Shemu day 9 of Ramesses II, generally dated to May 1274 BCE'; 'Following the battle, the Hittites were routed, but they held on to Kadesh'; 'Egypt's sphere of influence in Asia was now restricted to Canaan'; Egyptian influence in Amurru 'seems to have been lost forever'.

region.text: Kadesh and Amurru on the Orontes

ledger.note: 1258: Ramesses II and Hattusili III make peace. 'An official peace treaty with the new Hittite king Hattusili III' in 'the 21st year of Ramesses II's reign (1258 BC)'; it 'concluded the borderland conflicts' without the page naming the border (the Kadesh page does not describe the post-treaty frontier).
c. 1213: the capital returns to Memphis. Infobox: 'Memphis c. 1213-1069 BC Dynasty XIX (from Merneptah) and Dynasty XX'.

region.text: the Dongola Reach, south of 20 N

ledger.note: By 1200: Egypt gives up the Dongola Reach. 'By 1200 BC, Egyptian involvement in the Dongola Reach was nonexistent'. The year is the page's ('by 1200'); the Reach as the region south of 20 N is the reading. The same page has Kush independent only 'around 1070 BC', so the Egyptian retreat is drawn in two steps.

1189: the Twentieth Dynasty begins. NK page: 'the Twentieth Dynasty (1189-1069 BC)'; Ramesses III beats the Sea Peoples and Libyans, then the costs of war 'contributed to the gradual decline of the Egyptian Empire in Asia' (no dates on the page).

region.text: Canaan and the Egyptian posts as far as Byblos

ledger.note: c. 1136: Egyptian Canaan ends. Ramesses VI page: 'Egypt lost control of its last strongholds in Canaan around the time of Ramesses VI's reign'; 'Egyptian presence in Canaan was terminated during or soon after Ramesses VI's rule, with the last garrisons leaving southern and western Palestine'; infobox reign 'c.1144-1136 BC'. The year is the end of that reign (my reading of 'during or soon after'). The NK page says only that war costs 'contributed to the gradual decline of the Egyptian Empire in Asia' and that 'Egyptian presence in the Levant is still attested as far as Byblos' under the Twentieth Dynasty; the Ramesses VI page adds that the finds at Megiddo and Alalakh 'do not necessarily denote any strong Egyptian presence there'. [Author fix me-03-b, 2026-10-18] Was -1077, confidence 1 (bridged to the end of the New Kingdom, page silent).

region.text: Gaza and Sharuhen, the Gaza coast at the north edge of the Cliopatria -1150 shape

ledger.note: c. 1136: the Gaza coast, the last Egyptian holding on the Cliopatria -1150 shape, goes with the rest of Egyptian Palestine. Ramesses VI page: 'the last garrisons leaving southern and western Palestine around the time' (reign c.1144-1136 BC). The page names no city; Gaza and Sharuhen (ledger -1547) are my reading of 'southern and western Palestine'. [Author fix me-03-b, 2026-10-18] New event so that the keyframe from -1136 no longer carries Gaza.

region.text: Lower Nubia in the Sudan, north of the Dongola Reach, up to the Egyptian frontier

ledger.note: c. 1077: Kush goes its own way. 'With the disintegration of the New Kingdom around 1070 BC, Kush became an independent kingdom centered at Napata.' Rounded to 1077, the death of Ramesses XI ('began with the death of Pharaoh Ramesses XI in 1077 BC', Third Intermediate Period page). [Author fix me-03-b, 2026-10-18] Viceroy of Kush page (tried for the thin item): 'The former Kingdom of Kerma in Nubia was a province of ancient Egypt from the 16th century BCE to 11th century BCE'; no year near 1070 and no word on who held Lower Nubia afterwards; the Buhen page is silent on the end too. The kingdom-of-kush dossier (af-01) starts in -1000, leaving -1077..-1001 without an owner: unresolved.

union.text: the Dongola Reach, south of 20 N
Gaza and Sharuhen, the Gaza coast at the north edge of the Cliopatria -1150 shape

minus.text: the Dongola Reach and the Gaza coast

region.text: Egypt and Nubia north of the Dongola Reach as the Twentieth Dynasty held them after Canaan was lost c. 1136

ledger.note: 1077: the New Kingdom ends with Ramesses XI; Egypt divides between Tanis and Thebes. 'The Third Intermediate Period began with the death of Pharaoh Ramesses XI in 1077 BC'; Smendes 'controlled Lower Egypt in the north, even before Rameses XI's death' and 'the High Priests of Amun at Thebes became the de facto rulers of Upper Egypt' (NK page). The NK infobox says 'Downfall: c. 1069 BC'; the Twenty-first Dynasty page 'Established: 1077 BC'. [Author fix me-03-b, 2026-10-18] Region text no longer includes Canaan (lost c. 1136, ledger above).

wars.name: Ahmose I's reconquest of Egypt from the Hyksos
wars.outcome: Theban victory: Avaris falls (the fourth attack) and the Hyksos are followed to Sharuhen, which falls after a three-year siege.
wars.note: Starts with Kamose's year-3 sortie in the Cusae-Hermopolis borderland (Kamose page, 1555-1550 reign gives -1553); the Seventeenth Dynasty page puts the Memphis capture in 1559, which conflicts.

wars.name: Thutmose I's conquest of Kerma and Nubia

zones.text: Nubia up to the Fourth Cataract

wars.outcome: Egyptian victory: Kerma destroyed, Nubia annexed c. 1504 BC and 'absorbed into the New Kingdom' around 1500; rebellions 'continued for 220 years until c. 1300 BC'.

wars.name: Thutmose III's Syrian campaigns

zones.text: Syria from Simyra to the Euphrates and Aleppo

wars.outcome: Egyptian victories: Megiddo (9 May 1457 BC), Simyra (1450), the Euphrates crossing (1447), the Mitanni army met at Aleppo (1445); Canaan and Syria pay tribute, Kadesh not taken in year 42.
wars.note: Years counted from the page's accession of 1479 BC. The page's war list has eight or more campaigns; only the dated ones are cited.

wars.name: Egyptian-Hittite War of Ramesses II (Battle of Kadesh)

zones.text: Kadesh and Amurru on the Orontes

wars.outcome: Drawn battle at Kadesh (May 1274 BC); the Hittites keep Kadesh and Amurru, Egypt keeps Canaan; Ramesses II and Hattusili III make peace in 1258 BC.
wars.note: Ramesses II's raids on Dapur and Tunip in his eighth and ninth years (c. 1271-1270) held ground under a year.

wars.name: Sea Peoples and Libyan invasions under Ramesses III
wars.outcome: Egyptian victories: 'In the eighth year of his reign, the Sea Peoples invaded Egypt by land and sea', and two Libyan campaigns in the Western Delta; the defeated were incorporated as subjects and 'settled in Southern Canaan'. No border moved.
wars.note: The page dates only the Twentieth Dynasty (1189-1069 BC), not the reign of Ramesses III, so the span is the dynasty's.

certainty.note: Every frontier is approximate: the Nile valley's desert edges, the Nubian posts (Buhen, the Fourth Cataract), the Canaanite and Syrian tributaries. The Kadesh page says the 1258 treaty 'concluded the borderland conflicts' but does not give the border, so no frontier is treaty-sharp.

notes:
Cliopatria row 'New Kingdom of Egypt' (-1500..-801, 7 shapes) is split: this dossier keeps -1550..-1077 (shapes -1500, -1400, -1300, -1240, -1150); -1000 and -900 belong to the Libyan-age states (twenty-first-dynasty-of-egypt reviews -1000, twenty-second-dynasty-of-egypt reviews -900), so the validator warns that two shapes here have no verdict: intended.
Page budget: five pages (NK, Ahmose I, Thutmose III, Kadesh, 21st Dynasty) plus Kingdom of Kush and the Third Intermediate Period, opened for counterpart events and shared with the 21st-23rd dossiers; Kamose, 15th and 17th pages cited only in notes.
Disagreements: (1) the Seventeenth Dynasty page dates the capture of Memphis and Hutwaret (Avaris) to 1559 BC under Ahmose I, nine years before the 15th and 17th infoboxes (c. 1550) and before Kamose's year 3 (1553) campaign that reached only Cusae/Hermopolis; the ledger follows c. 1550 and does not draw a Memphis loss in 1559. (2) The Kush page has Egypt out of the Dongola Reach by 1200 yet Kush independent only c. 1070; drawn in two steps. (3) The NK infobox ends the New Kingdom c. 1069, the Third Intermediate Period page and the 21st Dynasty page 1077; this dossier uses 1077 so that the successors start the same year.
Not settled (page silent, a gap-filler should open the Wikipedia pages for Thutmose I, Amenhotep III, Akhenaten, Seti I, Ramesses VI, Twentieth Dynasty, Viceroy of Kush, Egyptian Empire): the year of Thutmose I's Levantine raid to the Euphrates; when Mitanni took back northern Syria; the Amarna-age loss of Syria and the Amarna letters; Seti I's capture of Kadesh and Amurru; the end of Egyptian rule in Canaan (the last dated Egyptian presence); the loss of Lower Nubia. The -1400, -1352, -1077 events are confidence 1 or 2 bridges.
Counterparts without dossiers: kingdom-of-kerma (-2450..-1504), canaanite-city-states and syrian-city-states (the princes of Megiddo and the Syrian coast and interior), sea-peoples and libyans (no territory). Region names: none outside the gazetteer.
No infobox area exists on the New Kingdom, Ahmose I or Thutmose III pages, so no Cliopatria area could be compared (only a 3-5 million population for the 13th century BC).
